Reflection

  • Advantages: Data attributes keep small pieces of metadata next to the element they describe and make them straightforward to read through element.dataset.
  • Accessibility: Data attributes do not add accessibility by themselves. They can support accessible interactions, but use semantic elements, keyboard support, visible focus, and appropriate announcements as this demo does.
  • When to use them: Use them for small, element-specific values needed by client-side behavior or CSS. Prefer visible HTML for user-facing content and application state for larger or frequently changing data.
  • Validation and security: Treat attribute values as untrusted strings. Validate against expected values, avoid storing secrets, and insert displayed values as text rather than interpreting them as HTML.
